title: Rishabh Pant Surpasses MS Dhoni as India's Top Wicketkeeper in Away Tests
excerpt: The 28-year-old became the first Indian wicketkeeper to score 2,500 runs in away Test matches during the ongoing series against Sri Lanka, adding to a growing list of overseas records.
body:
• Rishabh Pant became the first Indian wicketkeeper to score 2,500 runs in away Test matches, surpassing MS Dhoni's record during India's ongoing tour of Sri Lanka.
  • The 28-year-old has scored six of his eight Test centuries outside India, maintaining an away average close to 39 — significantly better than Dhoni's 32.84.
  • Pant is also closing in on becoming the first Indian to score 3,000 runs in the World Test Championship, needing just 220 runs heading into the Sri Lanka series.
  • The milestone cements Pant's standing as India's greatest wicketkeeper-batter in Test cricket, less than four years after a near-fatal car accident threatened to end his career.

A Record Built on the Road

Rishabh Pant has added another entry to his rapidly growing list of wicketkeeper batting records. During India's ongoing Test series in Sri Lanka, the 28-year-old became the first Indian wicketkeeper to score 2,500 runs in away Test matches, surpassing MS Dhoni to claim a milestone that underscores his dominance in conditions where Indian batters have historically struggled most.

https://x.com/ani_digital/status/2091768255937712488

The record is particularly significant because it captures what sets Pant apart from every Indian wicketkeeper before him: his ability to perform under the most demanding circumstances. While Dhoni finished his Test career with an away average of 32.84, Pant has maintained an average close to 39 in overseas conditions, powered by centuries in Australia, England, and South Africa — three of the toughest assignments for visiting batters.

The Numbers Behind Pant's Away Dominance

Six of Pant's eight Test centuries have come outside India. That ratio — 75 percent of his hundreds scored on foreign soil — is extraordinary for any batter, let alone a wicketkeeper who combines the physical demands of keeping with the mental pressure of batting in unfamiliar conditions.

"https://youtube.com/watch?v=7631brP129k His away century count includes four in England — a joint record for any visiting wicketkeeper alongside Matt Prior and Alec Stewart."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=7631brP129k

His away century count includes four in England — a joint record for any visiting wicketkeeper alongside Matt Prior and Alec Stewart. He also holds the record for the most Test runs by an Asian wicketkeeper in SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand, and Australia), having crossed 2,000 SENA runs during India's 2025 tour of England.

In comparison, Dhoni scored just one of his six Test centuries outside Asia — a 148 at Faisalabad against Pakistan in 2006. While Dhoni's contributions across formats remain among the most impactful in Indian cricket history, Pant has redefined what Indian fans can expect from a wicketkeeper in the longest format.

From Car Crash to Cricket History

What makes Pant's record remarkable extends well beyond statistics. In December 2022, a near-fatal car accident on the Delhi-Dehradun highway left him with ligament tears in his right knee, a wrist injury, and severe abrasion injuries. Many doubted whether he would play cricket again at the highest level.

Pant's return to Test cricket came in late 2024, and he has been prolific since. He scored twin centuries in the opening Test against England in 2025, followed by further hundreds at Edgbaston and Lord's. His unbeaten 101 at The Oval in the fifth Test — a counterattacking knock that powered India's dramatic fightback alongside KL Rahul — exemplified the fearless approach that has come to define his career.

"Pant has already surpassed Dhoni in all aspects bar aggregate runs — almost always a function of longevity." — Wisden

Closing In on More Milestones

The Sri Lanka series presents Pant with additional record-breaking opportunities. Heading into the tour, he had 2,780 runs in the World Test Championship, just 220 short of becoming the first Indian to reach 3,000 WTC runs. He is in a close race with captain Shubman Gill, who had 2,843 WTC runs entering the series.

Another century in Sri Lanka would also give Pant seven away Test hundreds, placing him second on the all-time list for wicketkeeper-batters behind Adam Gilchrist, who scored 10 of his 17 Test centuries away from home.

India won the first Test against Sri Lanka by 165 runs, with the second Test underway in Colombo. Pant, who has been in consistently aggressive form throughout 2026, continues to anchor India's middle order as the team eyes a clean sweep before a packed schedule of assignments ahead.

Redefining the Role

For the Indian diaspora that grew up watching Dhoni revolutionize wicketkeeper batting in limited-overs cricket, Pant has done something equally significant in the Test format. While Dhoni's Test contributions were solid, his greatest impact came in ODIs and T20Is. Pant has made the five-day game his primary domain, averaging higher in Tests than any other format and delivering his most memorable performances when the stakes are highest and the conditions most hostile.

At 28, with potentially another eight to ten years of Test cricket ahead of him, the question is no longer whether Pant is India's greatest wicketkeeper-batter in the longest format. It is how many of cricket's all-time wicketkeeper records he will eventually hold.
